explanation: The statement equates `(SalemCircle.P alpha inside).reflect (inside.card + 1)` with `SalemCircle.Q alpha inside`, where `P` and `Q` are the library's own definitions ((X − C α)·∏(X − C r) and (1 − C α·X)·∏(1 − C r·X)) in `LeanPool/SalemTheorem/PdtSalemCircle.lean`. Mathlib contains no declaration mentioning `SalemCircle`, and no general result of the form "reflect of a product equals the mirrored product"; the only Mathlib ingredients used (Polynomial.eval₂_reflect_mul_pow, reflect_mul, eq_of_infinite_eval_eq, reflect_mul_pow-type lemmas in Algebra/Polynomial/Reverse.lean and Roots.lean) are generic tools, not this result. Deriving it would require the definitional unfolding plus the `mirror_P` pointwise identity, i.e. more than a one-or-two-line application, so the content lies in the library's own definitions and this is not a duplicate.
